referenceName: LUV Estate: architecture-led property and investment story

source.name: LUV Estate official website
source.sourceType: official direct real estate and investment business website captured in Playwright Chromium
source.rightsEvidence: Requester-attested clearance dated 2026-09-29 covers internal desktop and mobile screenshot retention, derived design prompts, and pipeline-model reference use. No source-owner grant was supplied or independently verified.

referenceDna.annotatedDescription: A quiet coastal film introduces a large serif statement with only a compact wordmark and minimal navigation. A clay-toned introduction pairs concise property and investment context with a wide aerial development image. After a bright expertise prelude, several image-led capability chapters sit on a pale surface with generous spacing and simple next controls. A two-part contact scene and near-black group footer close the page. Transfer the film-to-thesis-to-expertise narrative and restrained scene changes only. Do not copy the source's names, images, logo, text, marks, claims, palette values, property locations, or projects.

heroGeometry.alignment: small corner wordmark and right-aligned utility links with a left-anchored serif statement
heroGeometry.viewport: establish the property and investment orientation with one short thesis over an atmospheric still or muted film

navigationGeometry.placement: small overlay links along the top edge of the image field
navigationGeometry.mobile: retain a compact brand and clear menu while keeping the opening legible

typography.display: geometric modern sans with restrained editorial contrast
typography.scale: large two-line opening, small chapter labels, comfortable body measure

palette.contrastIntent: warm low-saturation scenes with controlled high-contrast text and buttons

imageTreatment.mode: slow architectural film and project stills
imageTreatment.crop: full-bleed landscape opening, wide aerial property view, then image-led capability moments
imageTreatment.focalPoint: hold the landscape, architecture, and spatial detail as the visual subject

servicePresentation.interaction: a short overview leads into image-and-copy capabilities that can be paged horizontally on desktop

ctaPlacement.primary: contact the real estate or investment team
ctaPlacement.secondary: browse verified projects or group services

motion.library: native video or CSS transitions with an optional short GSAP timeline
motion.reducedMotion: use an approved still and preserve every capability and contact link

mobileRecomposition.strategy: cinematic stacked image and expertise story
rules: replace sideways expertise movement with a vertical or touch-safe sequence
use a poster rather than requiring video playback
stack the closing contact text and client-provided image
keep body text and controls readable over warm surfaces

prohibitedPatterns: copying LUV name, marks, source media, properties, people, prices, claims, or exact trade dress
making an investment return, value, or performance guarantee
using a sourced investment chart as client proof
putting dense white text on moving video
replacing each expertise story with interchangeable service cards

requiredSignatureElements.description: Atmospheric architecture or landscape introduces the promise before details.
Capabilities are expressed as image-and-narrative chapters, not an identical tile grid.
A compact closing inquiry follows a small set of distinct proof or expertise chapters.

acceptanceChecks: The opening image has a static fallback and readable overlay copy.
The property or development thesis appears before a dense capability list.
Each capability has a distinct verified purpose rather than repeating the same value claim.
Investment language contains no unsupplied financial performance promise.
The mobile sequence stacks without horizontal overflow and keeps contact reachable.

review.notes: Official site identifies LUV Estate as a real estate and investment firm and describes its architecture, project, investment, and contact sections. Full-page captures were inspected after rejecting optional cookies. No broken images or page errors were observed.
